title: Learning to Discriminate Scene Structures Makes Self-Supervised Depth Learning Scalable
claim: Our method beats prior state of the art across datasets, gains from more diverse data, and generalizes to unseen scenes.
layout: 3 panels: radar chart and line plot at left, qualitative image grid at right
description: A three-panel figure. Panel (a), top left, is a radar chart over eight datasets. A large orange polygon labeled Ours encloses a smaller gray-blue polygon labeled Previous SOTA. Each axis shows an AbsRel value. Training-evaluation datasets are labeled in green and zero-shot datasets in red. Panel (b), bottom left, is a line plot of Abs Rel across testing datasets. The previous SOTA lines are shaded gray-blue, with dashed arrows marking the performance drop from mixed-dataset training. The Ours lines are shaded orange, with red arrows marking the performance gain. Panel (c), on the right, is a grid of two out-of-distribution scenes, one indoor and one outdoor. Each row shows an RGB image, a baseline depth map and error map, and the MaSS depth map and error map, colored with heatmaps. Ours is consistently highlighted in orange.
caption: Beyond (a) achieving SoTA performance across diverse datasets with a unified model, MaSS is the first SSMDE method to (b) effectively benefit from increased data diversity and (c) exhibit remarkable generalizability to entirely out-of-distribution scenes.
abstract: Self-supervised monocular depth estimation is appealing for its potential to scale with unlabeled data, yet existing methods often degrade when trained on diverse scenes. This study finds that, under self-supervision, models tend to encode dataset-specific structural biases rather than transferable scene geometry, leading to cross-domain optimization conflicts. To address this issue, this study proposes the MaSS framework, aiming to make self-supervised depth learning scalable to diverse data. MaSS introduces a dedicated structural representation pathway explicitly decoupled from contextual features, which is guided by a novel scene-structure discrimination objective to learn generalized, layout-aware structural representations for depth decoding. Trained and evaluated on four diverse datasets, both individually and jointly, MaSS substantially outperforms prior self-supervised methods and is the first to consistently benefit from mixed-domain training. Zero-shot evaluation on eight additional datasets further demonstrates its remarkable generalizability, particularly on those entirely out-of-distribution scenes. The source code is publicly available at https://mias.group/MaSS.
